episodes.200485: Isolated to scattered thunderstorms arrived into West Virginia on the afternoon of May 8th ahead of a cold front. Damaging wind gusts accompanying these storms resulted in downed trees and power lines across several counties in the southwestern portions of the state. In Mingo County, a Mesonet station in the town of Ragland measured a 58 mile per hour gust as strong storms moved through the area. There was also an isolated instance of quarter size hail observed in Logan County. The front slid through late that night and concluded the severe weather threat.
episodes.200488: A few supercell thunderstorms moved eastward from Mississippi across western Central Alabama, producing instances of wind damage and quarter-size hail across Marion, Winston, Fayette, and Greene counties. Meanwhile, a cell cluster moved northeastward from near Andalusia into Pike County, with the main cell producing up to golf ball-size hail near Hamilton Crossroads before dissipating in Barbour County.
episodes.200508: A stalled boundary produced very localized flash flooding as well as some quarter sized hail in central MA.
episodes.200668: Thunderstorms produced strong wind gusts and severe hail along the Volusia and northern Brevard County coasts.
episodes.200906: From May 5th through May 9th, a ridge from the south of the islands interacted with an equatorial trough to the north. This created high winds on the 6th through the 8th with gusts reaching around 55 mph at WSO Pago Pago. Total rainfall recorded at WSO Pago Pago was 12.62 inches during this time, including 4.93 inches which fell from 8:50 PM SST to 11:50 PM SST on the 9th. High winds also created minor coastal flooding and erosion along the southern and eastern coast lines. As American Samoa received well above average rainfall throughout the year along with this event, landslides occurred along some parts of the islands.
episodes.200922: Severe thunderstorms impacted Middle Tennessee during the afternoon and evening hours of May 8, 2025. With a very cold airmass aloft, this allowed for steep lapse rates which helped to set the stage for large hail. Several reports of large hail was received across Middle Tennessee with the largest hail of two inches being reported in Franklin. Additionally, severe winds also downed several trees.
episodes.201030: A cluster of storms in La Salle County progressed southeastward through the evening hours. These storms intensified and developed into a well-organized MCS with a maturing bow echo feature as it extended into northeastern Duval and Jim Wells counties. An uptick in radar velocity was noted beginning north of San Diego, TX around 8:45pm CDT, with large wet melting hail enforcing a notable stronger surge of northwesterly winds on the southern edge of the storm over west Alice shortly after 9:00pm CDT.||This southern edge of the MCS became the most destructive bowing segment through the rest of the storm's lifespan, resulting in numerous power and transmission poles snapped, metal building structure collapses, and large trees snapped and uprooted. Widespread wind speeds of 70-90 mph were noted, particularly from Alice to Petronila with a few locations seeing wind gusts as high as 115 mph. While we were unable to access the Petronila area to assess the damage further due to numerous downed power and transmission line, photos and videos shared with us suggest that winds in excess of 100 mph continued through this area as well.||Hundreds of power and transmission poles were snapped between Alice and Petronila. Most were snapped near the base, however a few were found to be snapped 10-15 feet above ground, indicating peak winds of 115 mph. In addition, roof damage was observed, along with several rolled over semi-trucks and campers. Overall, the preliminary path length is 54 miles with a max width of 16 miles.
episodes.201246: Steep mid level lapse rates along with sufficient instability and deep layer shear ahead of a cold front brought a couple of rounds of showers and thunderstorms to the region. Large hail and damaging wind gusts were reported. In addition, a tornado moved from Holmes county, FL briefly into Geneva county, AL before lifting.
episodes.201343: Several clusters of thunderstorms developed over the higher terrain and evolved into a larger storm complex as it moved east into the southwestern Piedmont and Sandhills during the evening hours. The storm complex produced a swath of wind damage from Randolph to Moore County, with scattered sub-severe hail reported as well.
episodes.201388: Showers and thunderstorms formed along a stationary front, producing heavy rainfall.
episodes.201419: SW steering flow pushed a more dominant west coast sea breeze inland over a moist and unstable airmass. Sea breeze and boundary mergers focused toward the I-95 corridor eastward where isolated strong storms produced gusty winds and small hail as they moved offshore.
episodes.201420: SW steering flow pushed a more dominant west coast sea breeze inland over a moist and unstable airmass. Sea breeze and boundary mergers focused toward the I-95 corridor eastward where isolated strong storms produced gusty winds and small hail as they moved offshore.
episodes.201421: A surface front meandered across the local area. This feature combined with moist and unstable SW flow from the Gulf triggered strong to isolated severe storms in the afternoon and evening. A gustnado in Baxley produced no damage.
episodes.201530: Showers and thunderstorms developed in a warm and unstable airmass.
episodes.201950: A trough pushed a cold front across the region, producing scattered strong to severe thunderstorms over the Stockton Plateau and Big Bend.
episodes.202001: A 500mb trough extended from Quebec southwest to the confluence of the Mississippi and Ohio Rivers around midday and pushed slowly eastward through the afternoon. At the surface, a weak surface low tried to lift northeast through west Kentucky, as surface high pressure built slowly southeast across southern Illinois. The greatest instability was a bit elevated with MUCAPE values of 1000-2000J/kg, which resulted in effective shear of 25-30kts. Numerous thunderstorms developed over southern Illinois in the late morning and moved quickly eastward through the early afternoon. With precipitable water values around 1.25, the main concern with the storms was brief heavy rain. However, one stronger storm produced heavy rainfall sufficient to result in some street flooding in Eldorado.
episodes.202002: A 500mb trough extended from Quebec southwest to the confluence of the Mississippi and Ohio Rivers around midday and pushed slowly eastward through the afternoon. At the surface, a weak surface low tried to lift northeast through west Kentucky, as surface high pressure built slowly southeast across southern Illinois and southwest Indiana. The greatest instability was a bit elevated with MUCAPE values of 1000-2000J/kg, which resulted in meager effective shear of 25-30kts. Numerous thunderstorms developed over southern Illinois in the late morning and moved quickly eastward into northwest Kentucky in the afternoon. Around 1500CST, a cluster of storms lifted north of the Ohio River into Warrick County, where it produced some large hail and street flooding in Newburgh.
episodes.202003: A 500mb trough extended from Quebec southwest to the confluence of the Mississippi and Ohio Rivers around midday and pushed slowly eastward through the afternoon. At the surface, a weak surface low tried to lift northeast through west Kentucky, as surface high pressure tried to build southeast across the lower Ohio Valley. The greatest instability was a bit elevated with MUCAPE values of 1000-2000J/kg, which result in meager effective shear of 25-30kts. Scattered showers and thunderstorms lifted northeast from the Missouri Bootheel into west Kentucky after 0900CST, and more widespread thunderstorms moved east out of southern Illinois in the early afternoon. One cluster of storms produced damaging winds and large hail over portions of Union County, while a second storm dropped large hail in southwest portions of Daviess County.
episodes.202004: A 500mb trough extended from Quebec southwest to the confluence of the Mississippi and Ohio Rivers around midday and pushed slowly eastward through the afternoon. At the surface, a weak surface low tried to lift northeast through west Kentucky, as surface high pressure built slowly southeast across southeast Missouri and southern Illinois. The greatest instability was a bit elevated with MUCAPE values of 1000-2000J/kg, which resulted in meager effective shear of 25-30kts. A pair of thunderstorms developed around 1200CST and quickly produced large hail and funnel clouds from the Sikeston area to just south of Cairo, Illinois in Mississippi County.
episodes.202045: Strong to severe storms ahead of a cold front brought impacts to trees and power lines to portions of Early and Randolph counties.  In addition, flash flooding was reported in Cook county.
episodes.202168: Thunderstorms developed along a stationary front across South-Central Texas. Some of these storms produced damaging wind gusts and heavy rain that led to flash flooding.
episodes.202299: Multiple rounds of strong to severe thunderstorms resulted in several large hail and a few damaging wind reports across the region on May 8th.  A high-precipitation supercell thunderstorm developed across the Brush Country/Rio Grande Plains by mid afternoon and held together while crossing through the lower/mid Rio Grande Valley.  The supercell produced very large hail across the Brush Country, then dropped a damaging microburst in North McAllen by early evening.
episodes.202399: A mid to upper level disturbance tracked east across the central and southern Appalachians, coinciding with the peak heating and instability during the afternoon hours. Some storms first developed along the Blue Ridge prior to the convection associated with the upper trough, while storms associated with the trough tracked into the area from the west during the mid to late afternoon. Moderate instability with MUCAPE in the 1000-1500 J/kg, and 0-6km shear was between 35-40 knots, with lapse rate increasing to 7 C/km by the afternoon, so all parameters for severe weather were favorable, and both wind damage and hail were reported.
episodes.202402: A mid to upper level disturbance tracked east across the central and southern Appalachians, coinciding with the peak heating and instability during the afternoon hours. Some storms first developed along the Blue Ridge prior to the convection associated with the upper trough, while storms associated with the trough tracked into the area from the west during the mid to late afternoon. Moderate instability with MUCAPE in the 1000-1500 J/kg, and 0-6km shear was between 35-40 knots, with lapse rate increasing to 7 C/km by the afternoon, so all parameters for severe weather were favorable, and both wind damage and hail were reported.
episodes.202462: On the evening of May 8th, a few strong thunderstorms ahead of a cold front arrived into southwestern Virginia. These storms had a history of causing downed trees and power lines as they swept through West Virginia, and caused similar damage in the town of Vansant. The cold front slid through the state late that night, bringing the risk of severe weather to an end.
episodes.202464: Strong thunderstorms passed through the area on the afternoon of May 8th in response to a cold front dropping down from the north. While the bulk of strong winds with storms stayed east of Kentucky, there was one instance of quarter size hail observed by a member of the public in Lawrence County. Storms continued to travel southeastward out of the area through the evening as the front pivoted overhead.
episodes.202575: A weak surface low rotated about the Mid-South during the afternoon hours, making very slow eastward progress. Pulse storms tapped into marginal instability and moderately steep midlevel lapse rates to produce damaging winds and large hail.
episodes.202576: A weak surface low rotated about the Mid-South during the afternoon hours, making very slow eastward progress. Pulse storms tapped into marginal instability and moderately steep midlevel lapse rates to produce damaging winds and large hail.
episodes.202638: An estimated 0.25 to 0.50 inches of rainfall occurred on May 8, 2025. A moped was driven into a low water crossing before being swept away into Lindley Creek. This ultimately led to a fatality.
episodes.202782: On May 8th, 2025, a stationary front was draped across the lower Ohio Valley. South of the front, temperatures warmed into the low-to-mid 70s, allowing for around 2000 J/kg of surface-based CAPE to develop. Effective bulk shear values were fairly modest, around 25-30 kt, across south central Kentucky, though they did increase to around 40 kt over Tennessee. Just to the south of the front, discrete cells developed during the early afternoon hours, developing rapidly as they moved off to the east-southeast. In spite of marginal shear, these cells became supercellular, producing severe hail across south central Kentucky. Mid-level lapse rates of 6.5 to 7 degrees Celsius per km, and significant hail parameter values around 1 suggest that the environment was reasonably supportive of large hail development. Up to golf ball size hail was observed across Ohio County and Green County, with scattered quarter to ping pong ball sized hail observed in between.
episodes.202840: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed into west central Arkansas during the evening of the 7th, as an upper level disturbance translated into the region. The strongest thunderstorm produced large hail to golf ball size in Crawford County.
episodes.202876: An upper low moving over the Midwest plus a surface low helped bring a warm and unstable airmass to the region. Supportive shear with straight line hodographs favored large hail in the storms.

episodes.202953: Scattered to numerous thunderstorms developed across southeast Georgia in the early afternoon hours near a subtle surface trough. A few of these storms became strong enough to produce large hail.
episodes.202955: Scattered to numerous thunderstorms developed across southeast South Carolina in the early afternoon hours near a subtle surface trough. The strongest storms impacted areas along the lower Savannah River, especially Beaufort County. A few of these storms became strong enough to produce large hail.
episodes.202956: Thunderstorms developed inland near a subtle surface trough and impacted portions of the coast and the adjacent coastal waters. A few thunderstorms became strong enough to produce strong wind gusts.
episodes.203245: Multiple rounds of strong to severe thunderstorms erupted across the Lower Texas Gulf and Laguna Madre waters on two occasions on May 8th:  First, during the mid morning through afternoon, then another smaller window during the early to mid evening nearshore, and around/just after midnight (May 9) offshore. Wind gusts in stronger cells ranged from gale (34 knots) to near storm (48 knots) force.  The discrete nature of the cells likely produced areas of hail, but there were no reports as of this writing.
episodes.203281: A few isolated supercell storms developed during the afternoon of May 8th. One cell intensified and produced a swath of significant hail along with wind damage on the north side of Starkville.
episodes.203364: Numerous thunderstorms developed across the southern Appalachians throughout the afternoon and early evening. Some of these developed into supercell thunderstorms that resulted in numerous reports of large hail along with isolated damaging wind gusts, especially across the foothills. Storms had a tendency to redevelop over the mountains and move over roughly the same areas, especially in Rutherford County, which experienced multiple severe storms throughout the event.
episodes.203733: During the second week of May, a nearby deep-layered trough and additional rainfall over saturated soils produced localized flash flooding from May 7th to the 11th.
episodes.204756: A few storms became strong to severe late in the evening of the 7th into the early morning hours of the 8th.
episodes.206929: A cold front was tracking southeast towards Kentucky during the early morning hours of Thursday, May 8th. But by the time it got into the state, it began to stall. It remained stalled, with a spot low across western Kentucky, for much of the day. It wasn't until about 0Z that WPC analyzed it starting to sink back southward again, quickly reaching the TN border just a few hours later, where it continued to sink into the overnight.  A upper level low and shortwave were also moving through the state during this time, amplifying the instability and lift in the warm sector - which is where eastern Kentucky was located. Hail seemed to be the most common mode of severe weather, not just in Kentucky but in sourrounding states to our south and east, with several 2 inch stones reported in eastern Kentucky.
